transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is that I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. It's really noticeable when I’m supposed to sit quietly and handle things... like paperwork, or when I need to sit down and sort out shared household plans. I just can't seem to stay settled.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that are difficult to stop?
No, not really. I mean, my mind is always going, but it's not like I get stuck on the same thought over and over. So, no, I wouldn't say I have repetitive thoughts like that.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Yes, definitely. Especially when I'm in situations where I'm supposed to be sitting still. Like, in church meetings or at family dinners, I'm usually twisting my wedding ring around, or... or bouncing my foot under the table. I just keep shifting around in the chair, even when I’m trying really hard to just look composed and sit normally.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

No, not really. I don't feel nervous or worried about things, if that's what you mean. It's not an anxious feeling... it's really just that physical restlessness I mentioned before. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel on edge.
Do you often act on impulse without fully thinking things through?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I usually try to think things through before I make a decision or do something. So... no, I wouldn't really say I act on impulse like that.
Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes?

Yes, I do notice that. Like, if I'm putting together a volunteer sign-up sheet or working on our household budget... I'll go back later and realize I entered the wrong date, or maybe skipped a line entirely. Sometimes I reverse numbers, too. It's frustrating because it happens even though I really thought I had already checked it over.
Do you have trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes at work or in other areas of your life, not just with tasks like budgets or sign-up sheets?

Not really, no. I mean, I'm not working right now, so I don't have a job where it would come up. It's really mostly just those kinds of paperwork things I mentioned... paying bills, doing the schedules, that sort of thing. I haven't really noticed myself making those kinds of careless mistakes in other parts of my life.
Do you experience restlessness or fidgeting in other situations beyond just sitting still, such as when you're doing physical activities or chores?

No, I wouldn't say so. When I'm up and moving around, doing chores or whatever, I feel fine. It's really just... sitting still for too long that gets to me. But if I'm already active, I don't feel restless like that.
Have you always felt this way, even when you were a kid?

Yes, definitely. Looking back, I can see it was already part of me even in elementary school. I was always the girl with the messy desk, and I constantly forgot to bring home permission slips. My parents would get notes from my teachers saying I talked out of turn or that I just couldn't seem to stay in my seat. So, yeah, it's been like this for as long as I can remember.
Do you feel like your restlessness and difficulty with paperwork and planning are causing problems in your daily life or relationships?

Yes, it definitely causes problems. The fallout has been that people at home and in my volunteer circles just can’t reliably count on me. I hate it, but it's true. I’ve actually had to step back from some of my responsibilities because I just keep letting things fall through the cracks, even though I'm really trying hard not to. It's frustrating for me and for everyone else.
Do you think your restlessness and fidgeting are more bothersome to you than your difficulties with paying attention to details and making careless mistakes?

I think the mistakes actually bother me more. The restlessness is annoying, but the careless errors really mess things up. 

For example, I’ll put together a volunteer sign-up sheet, or I'll be working on our household budget, and later on I'll realize I entered the wrong date, or I skipped a line entirely, or reversed some numbers. And the most frustrating part is that I do try to catch it—I'll think I had checked it over carefully, but the mistakes are still there anyway. So, yeah, that's definitely more frustrating to deal with than just feeling fidgety.
Have your symptoms, such as restlessness or making careless mistakes, caused problems in your friendships or relationships with people outside of your home?

Not really. I haven't noticed it causing any major issues with my actual friendships. I mean, my friends know I can be a bit scattered, but it hasn't caused any real friction or ruined any relationships or anything like that. It's mostly just the tasks and responsibilities I mentioned before where it really becomes a problem, rather than just hanging out with people. So, no, I wouldn't say it's caused problems there.
Do you think your difficulties with paying attention to details are more related to being easily distracted or to not being able to focus on the task at hand?

I think it's mostly that I just get so easily distracted. Like, if I’m trying to sit down and work on something at the kitchen table, pretty much anything can pull my attention away. 

A phone buzz, a car driving by outside, or even just a random thought popping into my head about what to make for dinner... it just completely pulls me off track. And half the time, I don't even realize I've stopped what I was originally doing until a few minutes have already gone by. So it's definitely the distractions that make it hard to focus on the details.
Do you think your difficulties with paying attention to details and getting distracted are worse when you're in quiet or low-stimulation environments?

Um, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed a difference, to be honest. 

It seems like I get distracted no matter what kind of environment I'm in. Even if the house is completely quiet and there's nothing going on, my own thoughts will just pull me away anyway. So, no, I wouldn't say being in a quiet or low-stimulation place makes the distraction any worse than usual. It just kind of happens regardless.
Do you think your restlessness and fidgeting are more closely related to your difficulties with paying attention to details and making careless mistakes?

I'm not really sure if they're connected like that. I haven't really noticed the fidgeting happening specifically when I'm making mistakes or losing track of details. The restlessness just kind of feels like a separate thing... like this physical need to move, whereas the careless mistakes happen because my brain is somewhere else. So, I don't think they're directly related, no.
Have you ever been unable to hold a job or maintain a role in your community because of your restlessness, difficulty with details, or other symptoms we've discussed?

Well, I haven't held a traditional job in a while, but it's definitely affected my roles in other areas. The fallout has basically been that people at home and in my volunteer circles just can't reliably count on me. 

I've actually had to step back from some responsibilities recently because I just keep letting things fall through the cracks. It's frustrating because I really am trying hard, but I keep dropping the ball. So, yeah, it definitely gets in the way of maintaining those commitments.
Have you experienced difficulties due to your symptoms in multiple areas of your life, such as at home, in volunteer work, and in other activities?

Yeah, pretty much. Um, like I was just saying, it definitely affects things at home, and it's caused issues with my volunteering. I don't really have a lot of other outside activities going on right now, to be honest. But for the things I am involved in... yeah, it impacts all of them.
Do you think your difficulties with paying attention to details are the main problem you're struggling with?

I'm not sure if it's the only main problem, but it's definitely a major issue for me. Like, I’ll put together a volunteer sign-up sheet, or I'll be working on our household budget, and later I'll realize I entered the wrong date or just completely skipped a line. Sometimes I even reverse numbers. And... I don't know, it's just really frustrating because I always think I had checked it over perfectly fine, but then those mistakes are still there anyway.
Do you think your difficulties with paying attention to details are worse than your restlessness and fidgeting?

I don't really know if one is worse than the other, to be honest. They both just kind of get in the way. The mistakes with details are definitely frustrating, like I said, but the restlessness is always there, too. It's hard to compare them. They just both cause problems for me.
Did you exhibit hyperactive behavior as a child, such as running, climbing, or an inability to play quietly?

Yeah, actually. Looking back, this was already part of me in elementary school. I was always the girl with a messy desk, and I'd constantly forget to bring home permission slips. And, um, there were always notes from teachers saying I talked out of turn or just seemed completely unable to stay seated. So, yeah, the restlessness and the trouble with details have been there for a long time.
